messages:
Mira Patel: Quick check-in on the postmortem action items from yesterday's outage — want to confirm owners & customer-facing language for the status page + whether we can share the RCA with customers who ask. TL;DR: owners assigned but timelines unclear. Can we lock those and pick status page copy?

Sam Ortiz: I have the remediation list. Assigned: cache-config fix -> @Jules, autoscaling rule gap -> @Dena, rollout gating for the model -> @Carla. Haven't set firm due dates yet.

Jules Nguyen: cache-config fix is about the TTL default being overridden by a legacy deploy script. I can own the fix but need a week to validate in staging (with load test). Can we set 2026-04-01 as target? :calendar:

Dena Alvarez: For autoscaling gap I'll add a canary policy and alert threshold. Estimate 3 business days. Target: 2026-03-29. Also flagging recurring pattern — this is the third time we've seen cache TTL + burst traffic combo in ~6 months. We should add a recurring-incident tag and an ongoing monitoring dashboard.

Carla Ruiz: For rollout gating I can add a pre-rollout traffic-shape test and a fallback policy. Need 5 business days. Target: 2026-04-05.

ops-bot: Action item created: "Cache TTL default enforcement" assigned to Jules Nguyen, due 1992349200.

Ryan Holt: Re: customer comms, Customer Success wants a short, clear status-page blurb and an optional follow-up email template if customers ask. Do we want to proactively publish an RCA summary or only publish once customers request it?

Dena Alvarez: My recommendation: publish a brief incident summary on the status page within 24 hours (root cause, impact, mitigation, next steps) and offer an "RCA summary" link. Full internal RCA (with play-by-play logs, perms, internal timelines) stays internal unless a customer has a legal/regulatory request and signs an NDA.

Mira Patel: +1 to Dena's approach. Keeps transparency while protecting sensitive internals. For the status page copy, here's a short draft — feedback welcome: 

```
Incident: Degraded inference latency for hosted API
Status: Resolved
Summary: A configuration regression caused cache entries to expire prematurely under burst load, increasing per-request compute and causing higher latency for a subset of customers. Mitigation: We rolled back the regression and applied a temporary guard to stabilize latency.
Next steps: Implement default TTL enforcement, add canary rollout checks, and expand monitoring. ETA for fixes: see action items.
```

Carla Ruiz: That reads well. Suggest replacing "a subset of customers" with an approximate percent if we can (e.g., "~5% of requests"), but only if Ops metrics are solid.

Mira Patel: Good call. @Ryan can you confirm the percent with CS/metrics by EOD so we can update the copy?

Ryan Holt: Will do. I can pull a quick query and confirm: aiming for EOD PST.

Sam Ortiz: I'll update the action tracker with owners & targets. Can we add a follow-up checkpoint on 2026-04-06 to review whether the pattern reappears after fixes?

Jules Nguyen: 4/6 checkpoint works for me. Also proposing a lightweight postmortem trend dashboard: incidents by root cause tag + recurrence count. Ops team can host.

Dena Alvarez: Agree on trend dashboard. I'll create a ticket and assign to Observability team.

Mira Patel: Ok — to confirm next steps: 1) Sam updates tracker with owners & DOE dates (by EOD), 2) Ryan confirms impact % and we finalize status page copy, 3) Dena creates trend dashboard ticket, 4) Checkpoint meeting on 2026-04-06. If everyone is good I'll publish the status page blurb after Ryan confirms percent. :white_check_mark:

Carla Ruiz: Sounds good. Thanks all.

Mira Patel: Thanks — I'll follow up with a short email to CS and the postmortem action owners with the timeline and the check-in invite.
